messages:
maria gonzalez: Heads-up — customer X signed the PO for Private. They want customer-managed egress + a BGP handshake. We need acceptance criteria for the networking side before legal signs the SOW.
aj singh: Awesome. Can we list the minimum network deliverables? e.g., egress IP stability, DNS delegation, TLS termination, and test traffic plan.
kevin lee: Also need clear rollback rules if customer routing breaks. If they point at our infra and it blackholes, what’s the mitigation?
sarah chen: For acceptance tests: 1) Control-plane connectivity over management VPC, 2) Inference traffic flows over customer egress, 3) Heartbeat + metrics visible in Console, 4) KV cache flush behavior under re-route.
maria gonzalez: +1 to those. Add: audit log export to their S3 and KMS encryption proof. Customer insists on HSM-managed keys at rest.
aj singh: Question on BGP: do we require full BGP peering or just static routes + NAT as option? Customer prefers BGP for failover. That increases our ops support scope.
tim o'neil: From ops POV, full BGP peering is okay if we restrict routes (only /32 next-hops) and terminate in a managed edges layer. Need to document which ASNs we accept and how we rotate communities.
elaine wu: We should create an onboarding checklist for customers: 1) Provide ASN + LOA, 2) Test prefix(s), 3) Contact for pre-cutover window, 4) Signed SLA amendment for network ops.
kevin lee: Acceptance criterion: during 30-minute cutover window, 99% of control-plane RPCs must remain healthy (measured by our traces). If below, we roll back.
sarah chen: Edge case: customer advertises overlapping prefixes with our public infra. We should reject and require prepending or announce only specific /32s. Document rejection criteria.
maria gonzalez: Security asks: customer-managed firewall rules could block our health probes. We require a permitted-list of probe IPs and ports. Add this to the SOW as a gating item.
aj singh: Can we automate a lightweight connectivity test? e.g., a script they run that posts results to a signed URL we create. That would be an acceptance test artifact.
tim o'neil: ops-bot: planned maintenance windows must be coordinated. ops-bot: automated note -> Please file a change with #eng-oncall 48h before any control-plane routing changes.
ops-bot: FYI: default alert runbook for customer egress failures is here: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/egress-failure (view only).
elaine wu: Docs deliverables: 1) Network handbook page, 2) Onboarding checklist, 3) Troubleshooting playbook, 4) Sample BGP config snippets for common vendor routers.
kevin lee: Acceptance tests should be runnable from both sides. We own a test harness: 
```
# curl from customer bastion to inference endpoint
curl -I https://inference.redwood-cust.example/healthz
```
And they must be able to reach the same endpoint through their egress.
sarah chen: Add perf acceptance: p50 latency delta between hosted vs private must be < 20% under baseline load, otherwise flag for tuning/quantization tradeoffs.
maria gonzalez: Timeline ask from Sales: deliver docs + acceptance checklist within 10 business days. Is that realistic?
aj singh: Tight but doable if we split tasks: tim handles runbooks + runbook automation, kevin + sarah own test harness, elaine writes customer checklist and LOA template. I'll coordinate edits.
kevin lee: FYI — we need a canary policy if the customer wants to flip traffic gradually. Add an acceptance step: 5% traffic for 24h, 25% for 24h, then 100% after 72h with success metrics.
maria gonzalez: Approval needed: product to sign off on acceptance criteria, security to approve KMS/HSM flow, and eng-ops to verify runbooks.
elaine wu: I'll draft the PRD section for networking acceptance and post a link here when ready.
aj singh: One last edge-case: if customer egress has variable IPs (CGNAT) we need a plan — either require static NAT or use a TLS mutual-auth fallback. Add to acceptance: stable source IP or mTLS.
maria gonzalez: Great. Action items: elaine draft checklist (due +5 days), tim produce runbook + ops automation (due +7), kevin/sarah deliver test harness + perf baseline (due +7). I'll circulate PRD stub to product for sign-off by end of week.
ops-bot: Reminder queued -> weekly follow-up meeting scheduled Friday 10:00 for "Private egress acceptance".
aj singh: Thanks everyone. If we can get these doc links into the SOW, legal should be happy.
maria gonzalez: Thanks — filing this as a thread for traceability.
